main_text.p: rum potius habendum: altera in alia omnia iret, statuens, à legibus, factheris bus, juris jurandi religione non esse discedendum, moneretque populum, haud facile horum quicquam transgressione violandum: Et hanc vulgo Achæorum gratiorem esse, majoresque applausus invenire: ita fieri, ut qui partium Romanorum sint, apud vulgum jaceant despecti, & calumniis quoque sint obnoxii: alteri gloria & honore floreant. Quod si senatus velit, posse eum hæc quàm celerrime mutare. Nam si vel leviter significarit, istuc animos se advertere, confestim rempublicam gerentes ad partes Romanorum transitu-ros, & plebem præ metu exemplum eorum secuturam. Si autem hoc facere senatus neglexerit, sine dubio, qui jam adhuc partium Romanorum sint, ad factionem adversam concessuros, in qua paratam laudem & opinionem honestatis apud vulgum sint habituri: Et jam[illegible, ~3 letters] nunc videre licere, nonnullos maximos honores in civitatibus suis esse consecutos, & gloria florere, qui nihil aliud ad petendos magistratus attulerint, quàm quòd se quàm maximè strenuè petitioni & voluntati senatus diceren-tur oppositle, & leges patriæ decreta[illegible, ~2 letters] que facta defendisse. Quæ si placerent[illegible, ~3 letters]

page.notes: Right-margin notes are faint and partly under the text at the foot; they are not legible letter by letter, so each is marked illegible. The first word "rum" is a fragment carried over from the previous page. The catchword at the foot right is overlapped by a note and is only partly readable. The text "factheris bus" is a line-end split of "factio-" and "ribus" in the scan; the reading "factionibus" is not clearly visible, so the transcription keeps the printed spacing as far as it is legible. Long s has been normalised to s. The show-through and the reddish edge on the right are not transcribed.
